correctness.rationale: The segment inequality on each I_n and local unweighted integrability of the upper gradient give continuity there (and force pointwise finiteness there). For alpha >= 1 the weighted masses of I_n are bounded below by log(2); integrability forces the component minima of |u| to tend to zero. Also x^(-alpha) >= 1 on P without 0, so ordinary Hölder for p > 1 gives osc(u|I_n) <= |I_n|^(1-1/p) ||g||_X; for p=1 the gradient mass of each I_n tends to zero. This proves uniform vanishing and permits the choice u(0)=0. For alpha < 1 the total weighted mass is finite and the alternating component indicator has upper gradient zero, since every curve remains in one component. A continuous a.e.-equal representative must agree identically on each I_n. This verifies both directions at all stated p and alpha with no numerical dependency.
